summary: Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929). He held posts at Kyoto University (~1935–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo, his posts included the University of Tokyo, Tsurumi University Junior College, Tsurumi Women's University, and ICPBS.

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1985–1989), later holding posts at Hokkaido University (~1996–2006), Tohoku University (~2006–2020), and Toyo Bunko (~2020).

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu at the University of Tokyo and at the University of Vienna. He held faculty posts at Nagoya, Tokyo, and Hosei universities.

Klaus Bruhn was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg (~1949–1964) and served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin (~1966–1993).

Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Friedrich Wilhelm at the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich, the Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University, and the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Fischer was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University, under J. N. Banerjea and O. C. Gangoly (1952), and at Kabul University. He held posts at DAI and the University of Bonn (1966–1985).

Klaus Hahlweg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Helmut Hoffmann (completed 1954) and under Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Klaus Karttunen is an Indologist, historian, and linguist. Educated at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto, Asko Parpola, and others, he served at Helsinki as Acting Professor of Indology (1982) and Docent (1990, 1994, 2006–2011).

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Halle, Frankfurt, Göttingen (under Paul Thieme), and Tübingen. He held posts at Göttingen, Tübingen, and served as Professor of Indology at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Matzel was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Halle, Leipzig, Jena, Humboldt, FU Berlin, and Würzburg. He taught at FU Berlin and Peradeniya before serving as Professor of Germanic Philology at Regensburg (1968–1989).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg under Friedrich Weller and Karl Ammer, and at Leipzig. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig (1970–1991), Bayreuth, Göttingen (~1995), and Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a postdoctoral teaching post there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn is a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen under Spuler, Lentz, and Gabain, he held professorships at the University of Giessen (1972) and University of Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied at the University of Bonn under Paul Hacker and at the University of Münster (PhD 1968). He held successive academic positions at Münster, becoming ordinary professor in 1980.
Klaus Strunk was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1950–1957). He held professorial posts at Saarland University (~1968–1977) and the University of Munich (~1977–1998).

Klaus Wille is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. His career includes posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bonn, Marburg, and Hamburg under Michael Hahn and Klaus Sagaster. He held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, Hamburg, Vienna, and Hong Kong.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at PTH Benediktbeuern (1966–1971) and earned his doctorate in theology at the University of Munich (1978–1984), where he served as a lecturer in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Uppsala University in 2000 under the supervision of Peter Schalk.
